chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

I said, “May Allah keep you well! We gather together and discuss what is with us. Nothing is brought to us except that we have something written regarding it, and that is from what Allah has bestowed upon us through you. Then a small matter comes to us for which we have nothing, so some of us look to others, while we have something resembling it, and we make analogy according to what seems best of it.”
So he said, “What have you to do with analogy? Those before you were only destroyed by analogy.”
Then he said, “When there comes to you that which you know, then speak by it; and if there comes to you that which you do not know, then—” and he gestured with his hand toward his mouth.
Then he said, “May Allah curse Abū Ḥanīfah. He used to say: ‘ʿAlī said, and I say; and the Companions said, and I say.’”

Then he said, “Did you use to sit with him?” I said, “No, but this is his speech.” Then I said, “May Allah keep you well! Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bring the people what would suffice them in his time?” He said, “Yes, and what they would need until the Day of Judgment.” I said, “So has anything of that been lost?” He said, “No, it is with its أهل.”

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: its rightful possessors, namely those entrusted with this knowledge
key_terms.الصَّحَابَةُ: the Companions, mentioned here in reported speech
key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: analogy used as an independent method of deriving rulings
key_terms.مَا تَعْلَمُونَ: that which is known with certainty from transmitted guidance
key_terms.مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ: that which is not known and should not be spoken about without knowledge
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, marking the enduring sufficiency of revealed guidance

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about qiyās and the source of religious knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith forbids resorting to qiyās when no explicit teaching is known, and instructs believers to speak only on what they know from the transmitted guidance. It also affirms that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله conveyed all that the community would need until the Day of Judgment, and that this knowledge remains with its rightful أهل.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! We tend to gather, so we discuss what is with us. So there is nothing which is referred to us except that with us there is something explaining it, and that through you<sup>asws</sup> - what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Favoured with upon you. Then something small gets referred to us, and there is nothing with us regarding it. So we exchange views with each other of what is with us (and come up with that) what resembles it. So we analogise upon the best of it’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is to you and the analogies?
But rather, the ones from before you were destroyed due to the analogies’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘When there comes to you (a matter) which you know (from us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>), so speak with it, but if there comes to you that which you do not know, so Shush!’ (keep quiet), and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> gestured by his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> to his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> mouth.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Curse Abu Haneefa! He was saying, ‘Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said, and I say, and the companions said (but my opinion is better)’. 
Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘You used to sit with him?’

So I said, ‘No, but this is (indeed) his speech’. Then I said, ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Keep you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> well! The people came to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> with what they used to suffice with during his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> era’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and whatever they would be needy to up to the Day of Judgment’. So I said, ‘So, is anything lost from that?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘No. It is with its rightful ones<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Sum‘a ibn Mihran who has said the following.

“I said to (Imam) abu al-Hassan (a.s.), ‘May Allah keep you well, in our meetings we discuss the issues and find out that for almost every thing there is something in writing with us and that is all because of the blessings of your existence among us. We only find few small things for which we do not find any thing in writing we look on each other and we find certain issues similar to it then we use analogy in its best form.”
The Imam said, “What do you have to do with analogy? Many people before have been destroyed because of analogy.”

The Imam then said, “When you face an issue and know he rule about it deal with accordingly and if you would have no knowledge about its rule then this. He pointed to his own mouth, meaning thereby; this will give you the answer.”
The Imam then said, “May Allah…? Abu Hanifah who used to say, “Ali said so and so, therefore, I said so and so. The Sahabah said so and so, therefore, I said so and so.”

The Imam then asked me, “Have you been sitting with him?” I then relied, “No, I have not sat with him but such are his statements.” I then said to the Imam (a.s.). “May Allah keep you well, did the holy Prophet bring in his everything that people needed?” The Imam said, “Yes, and all that they will need up to the Day of Judgment.” I then said, “Is any thing lost from it?” The Imam replied, “No, it all is with the people to who they belong.’”
